minutes.headline: Selectmen filled a Parks Commission seat and two Zoning Board seats; Keating earth removal renewals were deferred.
minutes.summary: The board held liquor and entertainment license hearings, interviewed two candidates for the Parks Commission and appointed to the Zoning Board of Appeals. It heard earth removal permit renewals, deferred the Keating permits for further review and approved a Powell closure plan. The town manager reported on state budget aid, the skateboard park and ADA planning, and the board discussed liaisons to other boards.

public_comment.topic: A resident presented a citizen's petition with ten signatures to restrict plastic bags.
Announced the Stillman fair on September 8th and a fundraiser for a William James College mental health referral service, with the school nurse.

what_happened.line: The Select Board deferred the Keating earth removal permit renewals to a later August meeting, after a workshop with town counsel involved.
The board appointed Suzanne Jewell to the Parks Commission by roll call; the minutes do not record an audible vote count.
Patrick Callahan was appointed associate member of the Zoning Board of Appeals, with four affirmatives and one abstention.
A motion to approve the closure plan for permit 54 as submitted was made; the vote was not audible.
The town manager said the state budget added revenue and paid for the Turkey Hill asbestos abatement, freeing capital funds for other requests.

why_it_matters: Earth removal permits govern gravel and soil operations in town, so the deferral leaves the Keating renewals undecided until the workshop and a later August meeting.
The state aid and the abatement paid by the state free local capital funds, which can change what other capital requests compete for on the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: An earth removal workshop was set for the following week, before the Keating permits return to the board.
Selection policy items were to go on the August 21st agenda.
